subject: Companion MAP & ops playbook — rollout, canary windows, eval cadence

Vanessa / Team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We signed this morning (woo!) and I want to lock the practical parts of the mutual action plan: rollout windows, canary approach, migration steps, and training for our ops & clinical teams. High-level asks:

- Can you share a single doc that includes a timeline + acceptance criteria for each phase? (we prefer week-based milestones)
- Recommended canary traffic percentage and rollback gates
- Eval scenarios we should run against our test dataset before canary
- Training plan for 25 super-users + internal docs for future hires

We'll need this for our steering committee on 11/30. Also looping Tom (ops) who will own scheduling constraints.

Claire
Director, Delivery
Arcadia Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Kickoff: post-signature MAP and operational handoff

Claire — congrats on the close, and welcome aboard.

I attached a "companion" version of the MAP (companion-map-v1.xlsx) that embeds the implementation plan alongside the commercial milestones. Summary here:

- Week 0–1 (Dec 1–7): Provisioning + network checks (private endpoint, VPC peering), smoke tests — acceptance gate: infra green with <300ms median RT for sample requests.
- Week 2 (Dec 8–14): Small-scale canary (1% production-like traffic from internal test clients) — rollback gate: >2% error rate or model-output drift per eval.
- Week 3–4 (Dec 15–28): Canary expansion to 10% with staggered cohorts; run full eval suite (see eval-scenarios tab).
- Week 5 (Jan 4–8): Full cutover, final training week with on-site (or live webinar) sessions for super-users.

Recommended canary profile: start 1% then 5% then 10% over three business days each, with 24–48 hour observation windows. We will instrument alerting for latency, error rate, and a small quality probe set mapped to your clinical intents.

I also attached a preliminary training syllabus (training-syllabus.pdf) and flagged the eval scenarios we think matter. Laura will own the runbook and Ben will own training logistics.

Next steps: 1) confirm the committee date/time for the 11/30 steering review, 2) Laura and Ben to propose exact dates for on-site sessions, 3) Arcadia to provide a short sample dataset for canary vetting (PII-free).

—Vanessa
Senior Manager, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0183

Attachments: companion-map-v1.xlsx, training-syllabus.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Thanks Vanessa — quick notes from runbook POV:

- Acceptance criteria should include both infra (latency/error) and quality checks (precision/recall on the probe set). I'll add a short checklist in the companion MAP under the "Acceptance" column.
- Canary windows: prefer 48-hour observation per increment for our support rotation; that gives us two daily passes to validate metrics.
- Migration approach: blue/green with traffic-shift ramping; we'll maintain the previous model variant for 14 days post-cutover as a safety net.

I'll update the workbook with the checklist and a step-by-step pre-cutover checklist by EOD Wed. Ben — can you confirm trainer availability for the week of Jan 4?

Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding trainer/enablement details —

- We will run two 90-min live sessions (Day 1: Product & operations; Day 2: Admins & troubleshooting). Each session includes a hands-on lab keyed to your test environment.
- Pre-reads: a 20-minute recorded primer + quickstart playbook I'll attach in the next update (eval-scenarios-v2.md also included — this contains the probe queries, failure-mode examples, and expected outputs).
- For the 25 super-users we recommend breaking into 3 cohorts to keep labs small (8–9 people each).

Claire — do you have preferred weekdays for on-site? If not, we propose Tue/Wed of Jan 5–6 to minimize production impact.
